title: Polynomial-time computability of the word-validity test
statement: The Boolean-valued function that maps a bit string $D$ to the one-bit string whose bit is the result of the following test is computable in polynomial time: extract $s_N,s_I,s_W$ by the successive total first-projection operations specified above, let $n$ and $i$ be the lengths of $s_N$ and $s_I$, respectively, and test whether $s_W$ begins with $1$ and satisfies at least one of these conditions: it is tagged as a variable, its body contains a $0$, and the first argument extracted from the body has length less than $n$; it is tagged as the constant $1$; or it is tagged as addition, subtraction, or multiplication, its body and middle word each contain a $0$, and both extracted argument lengths are less than $i$.
